extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (URF) scheme (prospective fellowship applicants and their host organisations)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the Royal Society University Research Fellowship scheme, including document formatting, content required in each application section, ethical and data requirements, budget justifications, and participant/host organisation responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant completion and organisational approval by deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants must mark their sections of the application as ‘complete’ and the UK Host Organisation approver must approve the completed application by the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referring and supporting participants are recommended to fulfil their requirements at least 5 working days before the submission deadline to ensure sufficient time for organisational approval. The Lead Applicant must check the status of participants under the ‘Participants’ tab and applications submitted after the deadline will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility for liaising with approver, Head of Department and Nominated Referee
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the applicant’s responsibility to liaise with the Host Organisation’s Approver, Head of Department and Nominated Referee to ensure required tasks are completed by the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Grants team before the deadline if there is any issue. The Royal Society will not be held responsible for emails not received due to address errors or spam filters and no provision is made for non-receipt of emails sent by the Royal Society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-opening participant application sections
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invited participant accidentally submits their section prematurely, the Lead Applicant can re-open that participant's form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead Applicant should go to the Participants tab on the application summary page and click the ‘re-open’ button alongside the participant’s name to reactivate the form for amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support role (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: An optional Research Support role allows an individual from the UK Host Organisation research support team to review and amend the application prior to submission, primarily to ensure finances are recorded correctly for this grant programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This role is strongly advised for this scheme. If the Research Support Role section is incomplete, applicants can revoke the request via the Participants tab to permit submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of applicant data and possible data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicant data is governed by the Royal Society’s Privacy Policy; application information may also be shared with DSIT and Science Foundation Ireland and selected third parties for reporting, evaluation, or administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants will be contacted regarding award administration throughout and after funding; applicants may also be contacted by Royal Society, DSIT, SFI or agents for reporting and evaluation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When generative AI tools are used in funding proposals, applicants must ensure their use is responsible and comply with legal and ethical standards; applicants are responsible for the originality, validity, reliability, and integrity of any outputs created or modified by generative AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where generative AI tools are used, their use should be acknowledged in the application by naming the AI source and specifying how the content was generated (for example by listing the prompt used). Applicants should adhere to Research Integrity and Trusted Research policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications must be submitted via Flexi-Grant® (online only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can only be submitted online using the Royal Society’s grants management system (Flexi-Grant®); paper-based applications will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have not used Flexi-Grant® before follow the registration process. Further system guidance is in the ‘Systems Guidance Notes’ section of the scheme notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility requirements and completeness enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before completing the online form applicants must check they comply with eligibility requirements; applications lacking necessary information or evidence to show assessment criteria are met will be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are strictly adhered to; ensure all mandatory fields (*) are completed and required participant sections are submitted and approved before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID identifier mandatory at submission stage
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants should submit an ORCID identifier if they have one; this is a mandatory requirement at the application submission stage only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register for an ORCID at https://orcid.org/register. Data (career history, publications, qualifications) can be retrieved from ORCID to populate sections of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory fields and participants completion prerequisite for Host Organisation approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions marked * are mandatory. You will only be able to submit your application for approval by the Host Organisation once all sections of the application form have been marked complete and participants have marked and submitted their sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the status of participants under the ‘Participants’ tab on the summary page. Late applications or incomplete participant submissions will prevent institutional approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Career Summary content and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide title of current position, current employer and department, country/territory, position start/end dates, field of specialisation (max 20 words), and summary of current research (max 200 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain text only. In the research summary also include a brief comment on the strength of your current host organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement content, purpose and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement should summarise research career to date including research-related contributions, prizes and achievements, career and research aspirations, why the fellowship is beneficial at this stage, and how it will enable independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain text only, maximum 500 words. Use this to detail additional activities demonstrating contribution to wider scientific endeavour (conferences, patents, workshops, invited talks, public engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Career History requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a full list of appointments since PhD in reverse chronological order, indicating part-time percentages and dates; include any career breaks or leave relevant to eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth of information is up to the applicant but should provide strong evidence for academic merit. Dates should be DD/MM/YYYY (days may be omitted if unknown). Career history can be retrieved via ORCID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of COVID-19 statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary of how the coronavirus pandemic affected your research activities (e.g., delays in publishing, paused experiments, increased caring responsibilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain text only, maximum 500 words. Preprints can be included in publication lists where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Qualifications listing
rubrics_metrics.description: List all qualifications in reverse chronological order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth of information up to applicant; qualifications can be retrieved via ORCID. This represents you under assessment—include relevant evidence of academic merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key and relevant publications guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of up to 20 key preprints and publications in reverse chronological order, including authors, titles and references. Identify up to five most significant publications with asterisks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List should be three sections: (i) refereed papers in primary journals, (ii) contributions to symposia/compiled volumes (refereed), (iii) preprints. Provide full bibliographic references; preprints must state 'Preprint', repository name and persistent identifier (e.g., DOI). Publications will be reviewed on scientific content rather than metrics or journal identity. For multi-author works, clearly specify your exact role and contribution. Plain text only, maximum 1000 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Research Funding history
rubrics_metrics.description: List all current and previous research funding in reverse chronological order with particulars (type of award, value and title of research) and state whether these would continue if successful in securing the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note any pending parallel fellowship applications and expected decision dates. Plain text only. Data can be retrieved via ORCID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal start/end dates and duration constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships must commence between 1 October 2026 and 1 January 2027; the end date must be exactly 8 years from the proposed start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full duration is 8 years with years 6–8 subject to a mid-fellowship review. Year 1 = first year of fellowship from 1 October 2026 for scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title and scientific categorisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Project title maximum 20 words; select whether application is primarily biological sciences or physical sciences and select subject group/area(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select between 1 to 4 subject sub-categories to aid allocation to appropriate Research Appointment Panel and reviewers — choose only the most relevant categories. Provide 5–10 keywords to assist panel and reviewer allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a scientific summary of the proposed project outlining background and summarising aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain text only, maximum 400 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay summary requirements and audience guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a lay summary understandable by a lay person explaining why the subject was chosen and what is exciting, interesting or important, and potential societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel is experienced and broad; members will not all be specialists—this section is important. Plain text only, maximum 250 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal substantive content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposal should provide a detailed five-year project plan alongside a broader eight-year vision and strategy, including clear research objectives, description of experimental methods and techniques (including data analysis if applicable), indication of milestones/timescales, and broad long-term vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF upload: four sides of A4 only, portrait orientation; do not use text smaller than Arial 10; title and applicant name on every page; avoid security settings on PDFs and avoid fine-detail or colour illustrations because applications may be printed black and white. If using Text Field option, plain text only (maximum 2000 words). When entering plain text avoid symbols that Flexi-Grant® may not accept. Generate a PDF via 'print' to check appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named collaborators letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: If named collaborators are included, provide letters of support no more than 1 side of A4 each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should only provide information about the collaborator's role in the project and confirm their commitment to collaborate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Organisation and Host Department selection and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the organisation where the award will be held and provide the official host department name; provide a short statement justifying the choice of host organisation and how the fellowship will help achieve independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the host is best suited for your research and career and clarify how the fellowship will enable independence. Plain text only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and data sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Data outputs from research supported by the Society should be made publicly available in an appropriate repository and be made 'intelligently open' (discoverable, accessible, intelligible, assessable, reusable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Society does not prescribe a set format for data management plans — applicants should structure the plan appropriate to their research and focus on how data outputs will be managed and shared, stating repositories and addressing: what data outputs will be generated, where and when they will be made available, how others will access them, limits on sharing (commercial interests, personal information, safety/security), and long-term preservation. Outline plan maximum 200 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fieldwork documentation and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If fieldwork is proposed, provide details of location, duration and justification; upload mandatory documents showing local permission to travel/work and permission to collect/export specimens and evidence of deposit arrangements for collected specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload relevant files (e.g., permissions, letters from destination institution/museum) as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animals in research requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants proposing to use animals must ensure the use falls within the Animals (Scientific Procedures Act) 1986 and adopt the principles of the 3Rs (replace, reduce, refine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'Yes' to involving animals, it is mandatory to complete all relevant questions in the Use of Animals in Research page. The Royal Society recommends using the NC3Rs Experimental Design Assistant (EDA) to support planning; if EDA is used and a report uploaded, enter 'see report' or 'n/a' in fields that duplicate EDA content to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human participants, patients or tissue — ethics documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal involving human participants, patients or tissue requiring local ethical committee approval will be considered only when accompanied by the necessary permission certificate or proof ethical permission will be sought, provided in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 'Yes' or 'No'. If 'Yes', it is mandatory to provide either a certificate or letter as proof that ethical permission has been or will be obtained and upload the file as a PDF in portrait orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Organisation Type and FEC budget presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the Host Organisation Type (e.g., HEI, Research Council Institute, IRO) as different funding rates apply; complete the budget table with values at the appropriate FEC level (80% or 100%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgeting should be done in collaboration with the Host Organisation’s Research/Finance Office. Input values per fellowship year; note the full duration is 8 years and year 1 defined. The maximum award value is £1.87M. Apply a reasonable level of inflation except for PhD studentships and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and constraints on total grant and research expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the maximum award (£1.87M) there is no per-year limit on Research Expenses provided the total does not exceed the cap; funds should be distributed between fellowship years as evenly as possible; underspend can be carried over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total grant cap may be exceeded to cover visa/relocation costs if well justified. PhD studentship and fees are exceptions to inflation application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for salary and staff costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification for salary including grade and salary point as per host organisation salary structure and justification of annual increment; justify other staff costs including spine points where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include justification for any staff costs and follow Royal Society Grant Funding Guidance for required spine point information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for relocation and visa expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification including number of dependants (partner and children only), visa type, visa costs, and an estimate of other relocation expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that relocation and visa costs for members of your research group are not eligible. Relocation/visa costs may allow exceeding the cap if well justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for research expenses and equipment costing over threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully justify all requested research costs by referring to each budget heading; equipment costing more than £25,000 will require additional justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding will not be awarded without justification. Provide full justification (including spine point) for any other staff costs per Royal Society Grant Funding Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for inflation rate applied
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the percentage inflation rate applied across all budget categories and the reasoning behind the percentage used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No minimum or maximum inflation rate is specified but candidates should include a reasonable rate. The Royal Society reserves the right to reduce levels of inflation if not considered reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD studentship funding justification and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: If requesting PhD studentship funds, refer to yearly rates for stipend and fees in the Royal Society Grant Funding Guidance and provide a full justification for the studentship(s) explaining suitability and training offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total length of each PhD studentship must be 4 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant declaration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must declare they have read the Terms and Conditions of Award and agree to abide by them, have access to necessary facilities for delivering the research for the project duration, and have agreed with Head(s) of Department that they will be afforded sufficient time and resources to deliver the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms and Conditions for Royal Society applications are available online and applicants must confirm these statements as part of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominated referee selection and submission constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite one referee who can provide an independent, authoritative confidential reference and who is familiar with your research (e.g., PhD or postdoctoral supervisor or mentor); the referee must submit their reference by the stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominated referees must not be named collaborators, members on the assessment Panel, or members of the Royal Society’s Council. References must be submitted in English; if not submitted in English the reference will not be accepted and may render the application ineligible. You will not be able to submit your application for Host Organisation approval until the reference has been completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head of Department statement content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Head of Department must summarise the suitability of the candidate for the fellowship and the department, and the level of support offered to the successful candidate as outlined in the 'Commitments from the Host Organisation' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Head should also confirm the effective and transparent arrangements that led to the applicant being supported to apply for the Royal Society fellowship. Invite the Head via the Participants tab and ensure they can provide their statement before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: System guidance for form navigation and participant contact types
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the navigation tabs on the application summary page to complete sections; edit participant contact types (default collaborator) to the correct roles (e.g., Head of Department).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary page provides an overview including approximate length to complete each section and allows management of participants. Ensure the email address used to commence the application is the account that will receive all correspondence.
